turns.boundedConclusion: ZR 37-34 requires the specified transparency on a ground-floor-level street wall along a primary frontage, subject to its stated exceptions and ZR 37-31. This explains the rule only; it does not establish that the rule applies to the property.

materialChecks.criterion: The rule concerns the ground-floor-level street wall along a primary frontage and requires glazing with transparent materials, which may include show windows, transom windows, or glazed portions of doors; this is subject to ZR 37-31.

Transparent materials must occupy at least 50 percent of the street-wall surface area in the specified vertical band: from 2 feet to 12 feet, or to the ground-floor ceiling height if that is higher, measured from the adjoining sidewalk.

Materials counted toward the 50-percent requirement generally may not begin higher than 2 feet 6 inches above the level of the adjoining sidewalk. The stated exception is for transom windows or portions of windows separated by mullions or other structural dividers.
Transparent materials must have a minimum width of 2 feet, and no portion of the ground-floor-level street wall without transparency may exceed 10 feet in width.

The transparency requirements do not apply to ground-floor portions occupied by entrances or exits to accessory off-street parking facilities and public parking garages, where permitted; entryways to required loading berths, where permitted; entryways to subway stations, as applicable; or doors accessing emergency egress stairwells and passageways.

Under ZR 37-31, the minimum-transparency requirement does not apply to a commercial-district zoning lot less than 20 feet wide as measured along the street line, provided the lot existed both on March 22, 2016, and on the building-permit application date; it also does not apply to a community-facility building used exclusively as a school or a house of worship listed under Use Group III(B).

ZR 37-31 describes the provisions of ZR 37-30 as applying in certain areas not otherwise governed by ZR 32-30 and in conjunction with specified district, special-geography, or Special Purpose District requirements; these supplied provisions do not establish applicability to a particular property.

materialChecks.criterion: The requirements apply to discharge piping serving a pressure relief valve, temperature relief valve, or combination thereof.
The piping must not be directly connected to the drainage system and must discharge through an air gap located in the same room as the water heater.
The pipe must be at least as large as the valve outlet and discharge full size to the air gap.
The piping must serve a single relief device and must not connect to piping serving another relief device or equipment.
Discharge must not cause personal injury or structural damage, and the termination point must be readily observable by building occupants.
The piping must not be trapped and must be installed to flow by gravity.

The termination must be no more than 6 inches above, and no less than two times the discharge-pipe diameter above, the floor or the waste receptor's flood-level rim. Preserve that stated reference wording; the source does not select a reference for a particular configuration.
The end of the piping must not have a threaded connection; the piping must not have valves or tee fittings.
Permitted materials are those listed in PC 605.4, or materials tested, rated, and approved for such use in accordance with ASME A112.4.1.
